title: Re-pin an antenna's downtilt bracket to the marked hole
instruction: Reset the antenna's downtilt to the hole marked in green on its tilt plate.
context: Tower technicians set an antenna's mechanical downtilt by swinging its lower bracket to a hole on a graduated tilt plate and pinning it there; a wrong hole points the beam at the wrong area. Done by telecommunications line installers and repairers (O*NET 49-9052.00) and telecommunications equipment installers and repairers, except line installers (O*NET 49-2022.00). Board pin tasks hold a door or shelf still (the cage door bolt, the rack shelf pull pin); this one swings a hinged part to a chosen angle on a graduated plate, against gravity, and holds it there while a pin is aimed through two plates with 3 mm of play.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm); heights are above the table. Table: wood top; arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5) on its near edge. Mast: dark grey steel post, 3 x 4 x 30 cm (x, y, height), centred x 34.5, y 0, fixed, with a 1.4 x 4 x 2 cm bracket at x 32.3, height 26 on its front. Panel: white plastic, 2 x 14 x 17 cm, x 29.5 to 31.5, y -7 to +7, height 8 to 25, hanging from a hinge axis along y at x 31.5, height 26; plumb on a stop, free to swing its foot toward the arms (to 17 degrees), light damping; with the arm and handle it is 250 g. Handle: blue plastic, 2.4 x 5.5 x 3.5 cm, on the panel's left edge, y 7 to 12.5, height 8.75 to 12.25. Bracket arm: red plastic on the panel's right edge, 3 x 1 x 5.5 cm, y -8 to -7, x 30 to 33, height 4.5 to 10, with a 1.4 cm square hole centred 20 cm below the hinge axis (height 6, x 31.5 when plumb). Tilt plate: light grey plastic, 9 x 1 x 10 cm, fixed, standing on the table at y -9.2 to -8.2, x 24 to 33, with four 1.4 cm square holes on the 20 cm arc about the hinge axis at 0, 5, 10 and 15 degrees: centres (x, height) (31.5, 6.0), (29.8, 6.1), (28.0, 6.3), (26.3, 6.7) cm. The block above and below the 10 degree hole and a 1.4 x 1 x 2.5 cm tick above it are green; the other holes have dark 1 cm ticks. Pin: orange plastic rod, 0.8 x 19 x 0.8 cm along y, with a yellow plastic head tab 1.8 x 1.8 x 3 cm at its -y end; 50 g in all. Start: pinned plumb, rod y -13 to +6 through the plumb hole and the arm's hole (resting on the hole bottoms, centre x 31.5, height 5.75), tip under the panel's foot, tab at y -14.8 to -13 and 4 cm above the table. About 1/3 scale.
scoring: Grippers open at the end. T is the panel's tilt (at 10 degrees the arm's hole sits 3.5 cm toward the arms from plumb). 0 if the pin ends through the plumb, 5 degree or 15 degree hole and the arm, or was never drawn clear of the plate. 1.0 if the pin is through the green-marked plate hole and the arm (rod axis within 3.5 mm of both hole centres), T is 7.5 to 12 degrees, and the pin is not held up (lowest point not over 1 cm above the table or the hole's bottom). 0.5 if the pin was drawn out and its tip entered the green-marked hole by 5 mm or more with T 7.5 to 12 degrees, but the end is not 1.0. 0.25 if it was only drawn clear of the plate (tip 2 mm behind its outer face, or the pin lost off the table). Drawn out and entered are kept all run. Else 0. The pin must be drawn out 16 cm and aimed along y into a 1.4 cm hole, so pushing cannot score.
reset_notes: Let the panel hang plumb on its stop and push the pin back through the plumb hole and the arm's hole; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate: square holes built from boxes, a free hinge with light damping, a rigid pin with a head tab. The simulator scores the last step without opening the grippers, so a pin whose lowest point is more than 1 cm above the table and the marked hole's bottom counts as not placed, and a pin through a wrong hole counts at any height. About 1/3 scale.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (moved the right arm to the pin, the panel and pin stayed unchanged); demo: 1.0 (held the handle, drew the pin, tilted the panel, re-pinned, released and withdrew)
